outcomes.text: Use French spontaneously to ask and answer questions, express feelings, present viewpoints, argue and persuade, in speech and writing.
Use pronunciation, morphology, syntax, vocabulary and idiom accurately, including communication and repair strategies.
Understand main points, gist and detail in spoken and written French, infer meaning, and use and summarize information from sources.
Translate unseen passages from French into English and English into French.
Study themes and sub-themes in relation to at least one French-speaking country, using varied sources including online media.
Discuss the changing nature of the family: worries of grandparents, parents and children; single-parent, same-sex and blended families; new trends in couples.
Describe the cyber-society: who uses the internet, how technology eases daily life and what dangers it poses.
Describe voluntary work: who volunteers and what they do, and the value of volunteering for those helped and those who help.
Study political and artistic themes and sub-themes in relation to at least one French-speaking country.

subtopics.title: Artistic culture in the French-speaking world

outcomes.text: Discuss a culture proud of its heritage: national, regional and local heritage, how it reflects culture, and heritage and tourism.
Discuss contemporary francophone music: its diversity, who listens, and how to safeguard it.
Discuss cinema as the seventh art: why it earns that name, whether it is a national passion, and the main lines of its development.
Use actively and accurately the grammar and structures needed for the tasks, knowing forms and functions, with some items needed receptively only.
Know the AS grammar list below, building on GCSE grammar.
Use noun gender and singular and plural forms.
Use definite, indefinite and partitive articles.
Use adjective agreement and position.
Form comparative and superlative adjectives, and use adjectives as nouns.
Use demonstrative, indefinite, possessive, interrogative and exclamatory adjectives.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers and express time and date.
Form adverbs in -ment.
Use comparative and superlative adverbs and interrogative adverbs such as combien, comment, ou, pourquoi, quand.
Use quantifiers and intensifiers such as assez, beaucoup, plusieurs, tres and trop.
Use subject pronouns including on, direct and indirect object pronouns, and disjunctive pronouns, with correct position and order.
Use reflexive, relative (qui, que, dont, lequel, ce qui, ce que), demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative pronouns.
Use y and en.
Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -re verbs, modals and principal irregular and reflexive verbs; make verbs agree with subjects and use il y a and tu or vous.
Use impersonal verbs, verbs with an infinitive (with or without preposition), perfect infinitive and receptively dependent infinitives.
Form negative and interrogative sentences.
Use present, perfect (with past participle agreement), imperfect, future, conditional, future perfect, conditional perfect and pluperfect tenses, and recognize the past historic.
Use the infinitive, present participle and past participle, and verbal paraphrases such as aller + infinitive and venir de + infinitive.
Use the passive voice in the present tense (other tenses receptively) and the present subjunctive in common uses, such as after bien que.
Use all prepositions, simple (sous) and complex (au-dela de).
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Use negative particles such as ne...pas, ne...personne, ne...que, and ne with negative subjects.
Form questions.
Form commands.
Use inversion after speech.
Use depuis and il y a with time, comparative constructions and indirect speech.
Use discourse markers such as au contraire and en fait.
Use fillers such as alors and bon.
Discuss the positive features of a diverse society: enrichment from ethnic mix, tolerance and respect, and diversity as a lesson for life.
Discuss life for the marginalised: who they are, what help exists and attitudes towards them.
Discuss how criminals are treated: attitudes to crime, whether prison succeeds or fails, and alternative sanctions.

subtopics.title: Political life in the French-speaking world

outcomes.text: Discuss teenagers, voting rights and political commitment: for or against voting, motivated or not, and the future of politics.
Discuss demonstrations and strikes: union power, their effectiveness and differing attitudes to these tensions.
Discuss politics and immigration: political solutions, immigration and political parties, and immigrants' political involvement.
Know the additional A-level grammar below as well as the AS list.
Use dependent infinitives such as faire reparer actively.
Use the passive voice in all tenses.
Use the perfect subjunctive, and recognize the imperfect subjunctive.
Use inversion after adverbs.
Study either one text and one film or two texts, using unabridged editions.
Choose from texts: Tartuffe, Candide, Boule de Suif, L'etranger, Bonjour tristesse, Elise ou la vraie vie, Un sac de billes, Kiffe kiffe demain, Un secret, No et moi.
Choose from films: Les 400 coups, Au revoir les enfants, La Haine, L'auberge espagnole, Un long dimanche de fiancailles, Entre les murs.
Appreciate, analyze and respond critically in French to concepts, issues, form and technique, such as narrative voice or camera work.
Study one or two of the ten listed literary texts in full, such as Moliere's Tartuffe, Camus's L'etranger or Delphine de Vigan's No et moi.
Study one of the six listed films, from Les 400 coups (1959) to Entre les murs (2008).
Pick a subject or key question linked to a French-speaking country, gather relevant French sources including the internet, and analyze and summarize findings.
Present and discuss findings in the speaking assessment, without basing the research on the literary text or film used in the written assessment.
